questions.corrige_markdown: A chemical bond is the **force of attraction that holds atoms (or ions) together** in a compound or molecule. It results from the transfer of electrons (ionic bond), the sharing of electrons (covalent bond) or the attraction between metal ions and delocalised electrons (metallic bond), so that each atom reaches a stable electron arrangement.

questions.enonce_markdown: Using appropriate diagrams, describe how each bond type occurs in a named substance. *[15 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(The learner should draw the three diagrams described below.)*

**1. Ionic bond - sodium chloride, NaCl.**

Sodium (atomic number 11, configuration 2, 8, 1) has one electron in its outer shell and chlorine (atomic number 17, configuration 2, 8, 7) needs one electron to complete its outer shell.

Diagram (dot-and-cross): a sodium atom with its single outer electron drawn as a dot, and a chlorine atom with seven outer electrons, with an arrow showing the transfer of the electron from Na to Cl. Result: $\mathrm{Na}$ ($2,8,1$) $\rightarrow \mathrm{Na^+}$ ($2,8$) $+ e^-$ and $\mathrm{Cl}$ ($2,8,7$) $+ e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Cl^-}$ ($2,8,8$). Draw each ion in square brackets with its charge, $[\mathrm{Na}]^+$ and $[\mathrm{Cl}]^-$ (with 8 electrons round $\mathrm{Cl^-}$).

The ionic bond is the **strong electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions**; the ions pack in a regular giant lattice (each $\mathrm{Na^+}$ surrounded by six $\mathrm{Cl^-}$).

**2. Simple covalent bond - water, $\mathrm{H_2O}$.**

Oxygen (configuration 2, 6) needs two more electrons and each hydrogen atom (1 electron) needs one more.

Diagram (dot-and-cross): an oxygen atom in the centre with six outer electrons and two hydrogen atoms, each sharing one pair of electrons with oxygen (one electron from H drawn as a dot, one from O drawn as a cross, in the overlap). Result: **two single covalent bonds** $\mathrm{H-O-H}$; oxygen has 2 shared pairs and **2 lone pairs** (octet), each hydrogen has 2 electrons (duplet). The molecule is bent (V-shaped).

A covalent bond is **a shared pair of electrons** between two non-metal atoms; the molecules are separate small units (a simple molecular structure).

**3. Metallic bond - copper, Cu (or sodium).**

Diagram: a regular arrangement of circles marked $+$ (the copper ions, $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$), surrounded by small dots or $e^-$ moving between them (the delocalised electrons).

The outer electrons of each metal atom leave the atom and become **delocalised** (free to move through the whole metal), leaving positive ions in a lattice. The metallic bond is the **attraction between the positive metal ions and the sea of delocalised electrons**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give one property of each substance, stating how this property is related to the bond type. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **Sodium chloride (ionic):** it has a **high melting point** (801 $^\circ$C). The strong electrostatic forces between the ions in the giant lattice need a lot of energy to break. (It also conducts electricity when molten or dissolved because the ions are then free to move.)
- **Water (simple covalent):** it has a **low melting and boiling point** (0 $^\circ$C and 100 $^\circ$C) and does not conduct electricity. Only the weak forces **between molecules** are broken, not the strong covalent bonds inside them; and there are no ions or free electrons to carry charge.
- **Copper (metallic):** it is a **good conductor of electricity**, because the delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice and carry the charge. (It is also malleable and ductile because layers of ions can slide over each other without breaking the bonding.)
